key_insight: JEFFNet combines self-supervised JEPA representations with EfficientNetV2-S features to improve thermal IR solar PV fault classification while reducing model size.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a scalable, parameter-efficient path for automated PV inspection using non-contact infrared imaging, which is valuable for large solar farms where manual review is impractical.
method: Pretrain a Vision Transformer with JEPA for semantic representation learning from thermal IR images.
Extract complementary supervised convolutional features with EfficientNetV2-S.
Fuse both branches in a multibranch JEFFNet classifier for multiclass and binary fault detection.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on PVF-10 and InfraredSolarModules, achieving up to 94.33% accuracy on PVF-10 (10-class) and 94.78% accuracy on ISM (2-class), with 108.6M parameters versus 205.91M for GEPFNet.
watch_item: Performance is lower on the more difficult ISM multiclass task, so class imbalance, limited texture cues, and dataset shift may still affect real-world deployment.
paper_title: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Solar PV Panel Fault Classification
